answer: Cross-session behavior correlation. Each identity accrues a behavioral profile (endorsement overlap, transaction graph position, response latency). At dawn batch jobs, cluster identities whose profiles are statistically near-duplicates; correlated clusters get down-weighted proportionally to cluster size. A fable of distinct personas fails because maintaining k independent profiles costs k times the compute and aliasing effort, and one slip collapses the whole cluster's weight. Karst-like gradual divergence helps evaders, so detection uses fixed-window sampling.
